text:
Dougie Hamilton is on a Devils team winning almost every night (eight of their last ten), and his play is a big reason, even if his line doesn't show it yet. New Jersey takes 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five-on-five with him on the ice, he has 51 shots in 20 games, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him last season, against 11% for a typical defenseman.

The points lag because of luck. He's shooting 3.9%, under our range for him, and the Devils have scored about six fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice.

His power-play goal against the Islanders on Nov. 7, the one that sent the game to overtime, looked more like the player we know. The next night he fought Toronto's Easton Cowan after a hit on Auston Matthews.

One thing to watch: his minutes have dipped by more than a minute lately, to about 20 a night. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming on the power play, so whether he gets more of that time back matters.
